links.comparator_used: Discrimination (AUC) alone, as tracked across the same models and time periods
links.outcome: Detection of temporal performance drift in first-trimester GDM prediction models
links.effect: Calibration intercepts shifted downward from internal holdout to temporal cohort (XGBoost Δintercept -0.866; LightGBM -0.977), meaning more average overprediction, in all three models, while discrimination was largely preserved (temporal AUC: XGBoost 0.881, LightGBM 0.870, logistic regression 0.857). Logistic recalibration brought the intercept to about 0 and the slope to 1.0, and improved the XGBoost Brier score from 0.111 to 0.100.
links.tradeoff: Confidence intervals for the calibration shifts were wide. The recalibration was apparent (fitted and assessed in the same temporal cohort) and only partly corrected the drift.
links.quote: Calibration drift occurred despite stable AUC and was partly correctable by recalibration, underscoring the need for calibration monitoring before clinical deployment.
